chunks: When God promised you one of the two groups would be yours, and you desired the one that was not armed, and God wanted to confirm the truth by His words and wipe out the unbelievers to the last.

key_terms.الطَّائِفَتَيْنِ: the two groups (referring to the Meccan army and caravan)

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'one of the two groups' refer to in the context of the Battle of Badr?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the divine wisdom behind choosing the armed contingent over the unarmed caravan, illustrating that true victory lies in establishing the Word of God rather than mere material ease. It underscores the concept of 'Tawfiq' (divine facilitation), where God aligns human desire with His ultimate plan to cut off the heels of the disbelievers, a theme frequently echoed in the narrative of Imam Ali's leadership at Badr.
